youtube_video.description:
Read the full comparison: https://zudoworks.com/insights/mrpeasy-vs-katana/

MRPeasy and Katana both turn up when a small manufacturer goes looking for software, and both run bills of materials, stock and work orders in a browser. That is where the likeness ends. MRPeasy is a manufacturing ERP, priced per user per month on four plans, with production planning, purchasing, CRM and standard accounting built in. Katana is cloud inventory software for product businesses, with a free plan of up to 30 SKUs and one paid plan on a custom annual price that is not charged per user. This 50-second explainer sets out how each one is built, how each one charges, how both connect to your books, and which kind of shop each one suits. Every fact comes from the two vendors' own pages, read on 23 November 2026. We do not quote their prices: check both pricing pages with your own user and SKU counts.

Chapters
00:00 MRPeasy vs Katana: not the same job
00:04 MRPeasy: a manufacturing ERP
00:10 Katana: cloud inventory for product businesses
00:16 How each one charges
00:22 Katana's free plan: up to 30 SKUs
00:28 Raw materials count as SKUs too
00:30 Xero and QuickBooks Online
00:35 Which one fits your shop
00:42 Read the full comparison

Key facts from the comparison
- MRPeasy says it is built for small and medium-sized manufacturers and distributors of up to 200 employees.
- MRPeasy lists four plans: Starter, Professional, Enterprise and Unlimited. There is no free plan; the trial is 15 + 15 days with no credit card.
- Katana lists two plans: Free and Advantage. Free allows up to 30 SKUs, with unlimited users, integrations and inventory locations.
- A SKU means every item you track, including raw materials and components.
- MRPeasy lists finite capacity scheduling, production calendars and Gantt charts. Katana arranges jobs by priority and calculates material needs and timing.
- Both connect to Xero and QuickBooks Online. Neither lists MYOB on the pages we read.

The full guide also covers plan-by-plan features, traceability, the shop floor, a checklist before you sign up, and where ZMOS, our own job-shop software, fits and where it does not.

Choosing manufacturing software for a small shop in Australia, New Zealand, the UK or the US? Read the comparison and get in touch through zudoworks.com.

linkedin_profile_carousel:
I spent today with MRPeasy's and Katana's own pages, and the clearest finding is that they charge in opposite ways.

MRPeasy grows with your head count: four plans, Starter, Professional, Enterprise and Unlimited, each priced per user per month. Katana costs nothing while you fit inside 30 SKUs, then becomes one quoted annual figure that isn't per user.

So before any demo, I'd count two things.

First, every person who needs a login, office and floor. On MRPeasy that number sets the bill.

Second, every item you track, from finished goods down to raw materials and components. On Katana's free plan each of those is a SKU, and a shop that buys many different materials passes 30 quickly.

Then I'd write down the three features I couldn't work without and find the plan each one sits on. In MRPeasy, subcontracting, quality control and serial numbers start on Professional, and the API and webhooks are on Unlimited. Katana keeps its API and MCP server for the paid Advantage plan.

Both vendors connect to Xero and QuickBooks Online, so for most of the shops I speak to the books can stay where they are.

Those counts will tell you more about the fit than any feature list. I've laid it out in four slides, with the side-by-side and the cases where neither product is the right answer.
